subject: Urgent: Vanguard hybrid cutover - fragmentation / reassembly failures & anti-spoofing audit
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@vanguardhealth.net>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: netops@vanguardhealth.net
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uploads failing after cutover to private link

Hi Aisha,

We cut over our hybrid connection to Redwood Private last night. Since then a subset of large file uploads (20–200MB) from our on‑prem clients to the S3 backend via the tunnel have either stalled or fail mid‑stream. Small requests are fine.

Symptoms:
- Uploads stall around a specific offset, retry logic eventually times out.
- TCP retransmits spike; we see segment sizes > 1400 bytes.
- When we force MTU to 1400 on the host the upload completes fine.

We suspect fragmentation and reassembly issues across the VXLAN overlay (we're adding a ~50B header) plus anti‑spoofing rules at the provider handoff that might be dropping ICMP fragmentation needed for PMTU.

Attached is a short packet capture and a snippet of our xconnect config (no sensitive keys). Can your team triage urgently — this is affecting a post‑migration cutover for production customers.

Thanks,
Sam Park
NetOps Lead, Vanguard Health

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>

Sam — thanks for the quick heads up and the capture. Im escalating to infra and the edge team right away.

Immediate asks while we triage:
- Can you confirm whether ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation needed) is observable or being logged on your firewall? If not, we may have PMTU blocked upstream.
- Can you share the output of `ip link show` and `ip route get <s3-ip>` from one of failing hosts (redact IPs if needed)?
- We'll try a short mitigation (MSS clamp on the tunnel egress) while we root cause.

I'm looping in Karthik and Vanessa for kernel/egress and security group checks.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@vanguardhealth.net>, netops@vanguardhealth.net
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uploads failing after cutover to private link

Dropping in some immediate triage notes from the edge team:

High level possibilities:
1) VXLAN encapsulation adds ~50B so end‑to‑end MTU needs to be lowered (host vs overlay mismatch).
2) PMTU Discovery blocked — ICMP type 3 code 4 must traverse the path; cloud handoff or security groups often drop ICMP.
3) MSS clamp / NAT behavior: if SNAT applies twice or conntrack drops large segments, reassembly can fail.

What Im going to check now:
- Conntrack table size and retransmit/timeout stats on the SNAT egress nodes.
- Whether our egress path is doing a second SNAT (ephemeral port exhaustion can cause mid‑stream resets).
- Whether kernel offloads (GSO/GRO/LRO) are interacting badly with VXLAN. If offload produces > MTU frames post‑encap, fragments get dropped.

Suggested quick mitigations (can be applied as short‑lived rollouts):
- Apply MSS clamping to 1360 on the egress tunnel device (gives headroom for VXLAN).
- Temporarily open ICMP (type 3 code 4) on the provider handoff SGs and firewall ACLs so PMTU can advertise back.
- Increase SNAT ephemeral pool by +25% to avoid port reuse during high concurrency.

Please send the host ip link output and Ill validate offload settings.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Weve attached a short (60s) pcap focusing on one stalled upload; host is sending 1460B segments, then after encapsulation these exceed the 1500 path and we see "Fragmentation needed" responses on the capture end, but not reliably from the provider.

Also, our firewall team confirmed they have an anti‑spoofing check on the provider handoff that currently drops some ICMP. They can toggle it but will want Redwood to confirm safe windows for doing so.

Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@vanguardhealth.net>, netops@vanguardhealth.net

Subject: Escalation: schedule temporary mitigations and handoff windows

Vanessa / Infra ops — can you coordinate the following asap with a short maintenance window tonight? Vanguard will toggle anti‑spoofing to allow ICMP test traffic for ~30 mins. Proposed mitigations we want to apply as a canary: 

- Apply MSS clamp 1360 on tunnel egress interfaces in region us‑west‑2 (target: 10% of egress nodes first).
- Add explicit SG rule to allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 between Vanguard handoff CIDRs and Redwood egress NAT pool.
- Increase ephemeral SNAT port range from 32768–60999 to 32768–65000 and monitor conntrack usage.

Operational checklist:
- Pre‑change: snapshot conntrack counts, current GSO/GRO settings, list of nodes in the canary cohort.
- Change window: 30 minutes starting 23:45 PDT, ops lead to monitor TCP retransmit rates and 5xx errors.
- Rollback: immediate removal of MSS clamp if we see regressions for any small‑packet flows.

Links: INF ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7281 (live triage notes)
Attached: xconnect snippet from Vanguard (vanguard-xconnect-config-snippet.txt).

Sam — can your team be ready at 23:30 PDT for testing?

—Aisha

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@vanguardhealth.net>, netops@vanguardhealth.net
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: schedule temporary mitigations and handoff windows

All — post‑window summary: changes applied and immediate results.

What we changed (canary cohort → full):
- MSS clamping set to 1360 on egress tunnel devices (canary 10% at 23:45 PDT, full rollout by 00:20).
- Security group updated to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 from Vanguard handoff CIDRs.
- SNAT ephemeral range increased to 65000. Conntrack threshold bumped by 40%.

Observations:
- The specific upload flows that previously stalled succeeded in the canary cohort (retries no longer hit the timeout).
- TCP retransmits dropped to baseline within ~2 minutes of change.
- No regressions observed for small‑packet APIs; rollback not required.

Next steps for permanent remediation:
- Recommend coordinating a formal MTU alignment exercise with Vanguard to set overlay MTU expectations (we documented this in INF‑7281).
- Plan a followup runbook to make MSS clamp part of the private‑link setup if VXLAN is in use.
- Ops to open a PR for permanent conntrack tuning and update infra documentation.

Sam — please confirm you see stable uploads from your side; we'll keep monitoring logs for 72h and then close the ticket.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Edge Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
